Kill switch, step 1 of the desktop plan - the hook, with no OS firewall yet: IVpnKillSwitch (VpnServices.Abstractions), which the device holds (IDevice.KillSwitch, null everywhere until the Windows and Linux blocks come) and its VPN service host drives. The host puts the block up after taking the tunnel and before the adapter, fail-closed, and points it again at each adapter start (IVpnAdapter.Started, a restart's too, which may make the interface anew) with what the session's routes leave out: the device-level split only, as the app-level splits (country, IP via app, domain) go out as the service's own traffic. The switch applies to a session at once through the reconfigure (UseKillSwitch in ClientOptions and ClientReconfigureParams). The tunnel's holder replaces or removes any app's block; a person's disconnect and the switch turned off lift this app's own, and nothing else does, so an error stop leaves it up. A premium feature where always on is one (AppFeature.KillSwitch, in CONNECT's list); refused with a null-capture Tested: the new KillSwitchTest, with a block played in memory (TestVpnKillSwitch), the whole VpnHood.Test and VpnHood.AppLib.Test (but VpnTunnelLockTest's three OS-lock tests, refused the tunnel's namespace in an unelevated shell).
